column2: The computer was designed to enhance our lives but, instead, ended up being the ruin of us all."

We made the mistake of tying it into the most important facets of our existence here on Xenon including our weather control and defense systems.
278	It seemed like a sound idea at the time and all proceeded well for about three years.

It was around then that a deep space salvage operation recovered what appeared to be some sort of antiquated data storage unit contained in a flimsy cardboard box on which the words Leisure Suit Larry" were imprinted.
On its back was the picture of a not particularly wholesome gentleman, but that's another story."

My counterparts exhibited shameful behavior as they tore open the box to get at its contents. I could not understand the commotion it generated. The data was uploaded into the Super Computer for analysis.
282	As a result, a crippling virus spread through the machine like a bad social disease. All control of the computer was lost.
All screens went blank, then these words were displayed by the monitors and uttered by the vocal outputs - WILCO MUST PAY!"
Ah! A button. Perhaps I'll give it a press.

You've reached the Sewer Maintenance Office. Apparently this office has been long abandoned. Your janitorial instincts urge you to sweep up and do a little dusting, but you suppress those urges and concentrate on the task at hand.
The smell down here isn't as bad as you thought.
It's just an average old-fashioned desk blotter.
The strange little pedestal has wires running between it and the wall.
Nothing you can do to it here will be of benefit.
The desk is not exactly executive caliber.
This heavy gauge wire disappears into the wall.
They won't come loose.
You notice the shadow cast on the wall by the inaccessible grate above.
A variety of pipes, coolant and otherwise, pass in, through and around the room.
They're well affixed.

Hey, that looks like Vienna's Parliament! Not many people get a chance to see this before they die.
The stone structure vaguely reminds you of photos from Munich, where you've heard tales of beauty and mystery. Most people will never see such things before they die.
Isn't that Neil in Lucerne, Switzerland? What a good-looking guy. Most people will (unfortunately) never get to know Neil before they die.
Man, that was intense. Neil's Tip #37: Do things before you die.
You take the jar into custody.
There's a hatch here. Your janitorial background helps you recognize it as a sewer accessway. Your stomach churns just considering the wonderful things one can find in a sewer.
You realize that this is the only way out, so you decide to leave it open.
There's an open hatch set into a cylindrical structure here. You recognize it as the entrance to the sewer system.
You peer into the darker area beyond the hatch frame and see nothing particularly revolting.
It smells mysterious. You have the urge to play 'Name That Gas'.
It's an empty jar with a lid, neither of which does anything entertaining.
The manhole cover is getting heavy!
You slide down the slimy ladder as the manhole cover slams back into place.
The manhole cover is simply an incredibly heavy slab of metal trying to tamp you back into the tube.
A sleek patrol transport occupies the area presently.
If you can do anything with the ship you certainly can't do it from here.
There's that green building again.
That white building sits over yonder. You start to become properly oriented regarding your position.
The dank and slimy conduit calls to you.
Your head is unusually well suited to serve as a manhole cover coaster.
The only thing you can do to avoid flattening your head any further is get in or get out.
You have a low-level view of the street from your manhole perch.
There's a small vent set into the side of the sewer tunnel. Unfortunately, it looks way too narrow for a space janitor, even a skinny one, to squeeze inside.
This hatch, locked from the other side, was your portal to this area.
This hatch opens from the other side only.
Nobody can hear you through the thick door.
Oh, no! The door has shut and there's no way back... What are you going to do now?
A sturdy metal ladder is attached to the wall here. At the top of the ladder there appears to be something resembling the underside of a manhole cover.
Not now!
This must be Vohaul's chamber, where his dirtiest of deeds are set into motion. You can sense that this place is alive with raw energy.
You don't really want to go down there AGAIN...
Dang!
It's Roger Jr!
It's a disk drive.
It's a disk drive unit.
The ladder leads down to the floor far below.
The orbs crackle and sizzle with raw energy.
The orbs just seem to hover in mid air.
This is the top half of an odd I/O unit. It also provides lighting for the area.
The large pedestal standing in the center of this chamber seems to be some sort of huge I/O unit for the Super Computer.
Even standing on your tiptoes, you'd never be able to reach that with your tongue.
It smells like a desperate, sweaty maintenance engineer has been walking around here.
Is that the best effort you can muster? All this space hero nonsense must be getting to you. You're getting OLD, Roger! I, on the other hand, am enjoying the physical joys of youth.
You were nearly thrown off the edge of the platform! Be more careful!

Then he will be destroyed once and for all. Ha ha ha....

He had just aided Wilco in escaping.

HELLLLLOOOO!
It looks as though another unfortunate adventurer is suffering a similar fate!
You find yourself in a nest perched high above the irregular surface of this butte-laden planet.
The inedible portions of the pterodactyl's previous meals lie scattered about in the nest.
The skull would love to converse with you if it still bore the soft fleshy matter which once made it a functional head.
The huge nest is constructed of sticks and assorted being parts gathered from this bleak, planet. It is then cemented in place by a generous helping of pterodactyl saliva. Ugh!
Hey! Those talon things hurt! You didn't much care for the landing either.
You frisk the skewered Sequel Policeman and turn up a paper-wrapped wad of used chewing gum.
My, my! Rather than the Sequel Policeman penetrating the inner sanctum of the nest, the reverse obviously occurred.
What do you want? A bone marrow sample? You've already cleaned the guy's pockets.
Seriously, do you actually think this guy has time to talk to you? He's too busy being dead.
Right now the Sequel policeman has no distinct smell. But give him a few days and he'll be quite aromatic, not to mention plumped up like a ball park frank!
Take it from someone who knows sick. Licking corpses is going way beyond simple dementia. Grab a grip, pal.
You notice a small breach in the side of the nest.
Your hair is the last thing on your mind right now (even though it's on top of your head)!
You see a huge nest in the distance below you.
Wow! This bird could use some skin lotion on those talons.
You look pretty pathetic hanging under the pterodactyl.
Wow! What an incredible view!

All around you stretch the stony outcroppings of the Estros buttes. A slender spire of angry red rock arches its way upward, poking searchingly into the sky and plunging down into the beautiful canyons of Estros. What lovely scenery!
Whoaahhh! What was that?
It looks like you've got company Roger. Must be those armed tough guys you met on Magmetheus. Be careful!
You can't do that.
Sedimentary layers of rock form a stairway which winds its way down below.
Your high-tech but butt-ugly pod stands ready to ride the wild planes of time.
The smells of stressed carbon fiber, cooling engines and ozone fill the air.
Tasting the cooling time pod would not be a good idea.
The shale-like shelves provide a stairway to the unknown.
You've seen a lot of plateaus and sloping hills before, but this one's a butte. The entire horizon undulates in enticing peaks, curves and crevices for which Estros is famous.
You're surrounded by spires of sand and rock. The ravages of wind, water and time have exposed strata in the butte which serve as steps to other areas. Far below, the waters of Estros beckon to you.
A mysterious shadow quickly moves from your view.
